definitions.gloss: previous graduate; person who has already graduated
definitions.explanation: A person who has already graduated from school but has not yet secured employment. In the Japanese job market, this term specifically refers to graduates who missed the standard new-graduate hiring cycle.

examples.japanese: {既卒|きそつ}{向|む}けの{求人|きゅうじん}を{探|さが}している。
examples.english: I'm looking for job postings for previous graduates.

examples.japanese: {既卒|きそつ}でも{応募|おうぼ}できる{企業|きぎょう}は{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: More companies are accepting applications from previous graduates.

examples.japanese: {新卒|しんそつ}で{就職|しゅうしょく}できなかったので、{既卒|きそつ}として{就職|しゅうしょく}{活動|かつどう}を{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: Since I couldn't get a job as a new graduate, I'm continuing my job search as a previous graduate.

notes:
USAGE:
{既卒|きそつ} is a job-market term specific to Japan's hiring system. Japanese companies traditionally hire {新卒|しんそつ} (new graduates) in a standardized annual cycle. Those who graduate without landing a job are classified as {既卒|きそつ} and may face disadvantages in the hiring process, though this has been gradually changing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {既卒|きそつ}{採用|さいよう} (hiring of previous graduates)
- {既卒|きそつ}{向|む}け (aimed at previous graduates)
- {既卒|きそつ}{者|しゃ} (previous graduate — as a person)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {新卒|しんそつ} — new graduate (graduating in the current academic year)
- {既卒|きそつ} — previous graduate (already graduated, not yet employed)
- {第二新卒|だいにしんそつ} — someone who left their first job within a few years
